problem: Generalist navigation foundation models use monolithic observation-to-action policies that are black-box, are brittle when metric goals drift into non-traversable regions, and entangle open-vocabulary recognition with control (search vs approach), causing optimization interference across tasks.
motivation: Real deployment needs one model for point, object, POI, instruction and person-following goals, with safe, rule-compliant and auditable behaviour. Decoupling slow semantic reasoning from fast motor control through a human-readable bottleneck allows independent scaling of perception and control data and root-cause failure analysis.
key_idea: A slow 4B VLM emits a Chain-of-Thought plus image-space pixel goals (affordance and target pixels), and a fast 2B VLM action expert tracks these pixels to output waypoints, reducing all five navigation tasks to 'tracking CoT-explained pixels' with GRPO post-training on the slow system.
insight: The shared pixel-goal interface lets a single multi-task checkpoint match or beat per-task fine-tuned variants (ABot-N1 vs ABot-N1† on R2R-CE SR 70.9 vs 68.3, POIBench 77.3 vs 69.9, indoor point-goal 95.4 vs 90.4), indicating positive cross-task transfer. Slow-system commitment to a pixel goal makes the fast policy near-unimodal, so simple smooth-L1 regression suffices. Outdoor point-goal gains concentrate on the hardest tier (88.0 vs 65.3 for ABot-N0), consistent with affordance-pixel re-grounding to traversable regions. No isolated ablation of GRPO or CoT is reported.
method: Slow system: Qwen-3.5-4B VLM takes reference memory frames, tri-view (left/front/right) RGB, task text and its previous decision, and outputs a CoT (only for instruction-following and object-goal) plus affordance/target pixel goals.

Fast system: Qwen-3.5-2B backbone consumes current memory/observation, slow CoT and pixels, the reference observation and task; learnable action queries via QFormer cross-attention plus MLP decode H=5 SE(2) waypoints (x,y,sin,cos) with a completion flag, trained with smooth-L1 and arrival loss.
Asynchronous inference: the slow system runs at low frequency while the fast system continuously tracks the cached pixel goal with the latest observations, compensating for slow-system latency.

Pretraining data: 30M samples (13.3M slow, 16.4M fast) across 5 tasks from 800+ indoor and 22 outdoor 3DGS scenes, with expert and DAgger/OOD-correction rollouts, noise-injected pixel and target inputs (asymmetric for slow vs fast), and CoT flywheels; POI data comes from a 31M street-view pairs distilled Qwen-3.5-4B annotator (~3.0M slow samples with negatives).

GRPO post-training of the slow system on ~0.5M point-goal episodes: composite reward of format (gating), target alignment (exponential decay of pixel L2) and safety clearance (asymmetric exponential penalty from back-projected depth); balanced Safe/Critical/Danger sampling at 5:3:2 derived from a variance/GSNR analysis, with a KL anchor.
Benchmarks: ABotN-PointBench (31 real 3DGS scenes, 465 reference trajectories, SR under collision budgets) and ABotN-POIBench (11 commercial regions, 163 POIs, SR at 2 m of the entrance frame).
Real deployment: on the AMap TuTu quadruped with Jetson AGX Orin, a lighter variant (slow Qwen-3.5-2B, fast 306M DiT with DINOv2-Base) runs at 10 Hz.

numbers_note: Split for ABotN benchmarks and EVT-Bench recorded as 'test' since these are closed-loop eval sets with no official train/val split naming; the paper does not state a split. Real-robot results are qualitative only. No ablation tables for GRPO, CoT or the pixel-goal interface.
results: A single ABot-N1 checkpoint reaches R2R-CE val-unseen SR 70.9 / SPL 67.5 / NE 3.32 with tri-view RGB only, beating Qwen-RobotNav-4B (69.5 SR) and ABot-N0 (66.4 SR). It also gets 92.9 outdoor SR on PointBench (vs ABot-N0 76.9), 77.3 SR on POIBench (vs POINav 42.3), 84.9 SR on short-horizon OVON (vs ABot-N0 73.2), and 90.1 STT SR on EVT-Bench. On RxR-CE it has the best NE (3.13) but is second to Qwen-RobotNav-4B on SR/SPL (75.2/65.0).
limitations: No ablations isolate GRPO, CoT, or pixel-goal contributions; GRPO is validated only on point-goal, with extension to other tasks left as future work.
Higher collision rate on EVT-Bench DT/AT (17.9 vs ABot-N0 11.6 / 7.05); object-goal evaluated on a re-curated short-horizon OVON rather than the standard long-horizon protocol.

New benchmarks are authored by the same team and simulated in an in-house 3DGS evaluator; POI fast system gets no closed-loop POI training data; real-world results are qualitative only, using a smaller edge model.
